statusText: Green - every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at its structural floor while a fresh, unpriced Saudi energy escalation builds toward a reopen beyond this window

headline: A fresh strike on Riyadh and Aramco's Yanbu hub lands entirely unpriced across a fully halted weekend window, lifting late-window Stress while Tail stays at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the final observed futures print was not a session extreme - and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, four hours after the last slot in this window. No published hour contains a tradable tape. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The 10-year rose about 6bp to 4.997% and the 2-year about 7bp to 4.75%. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, a third consecutive decline. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional: semiconductors averaged +1.28% with MU +3.92% and ARM +4.04%, while software fell about 1% and megacaps split four to four with META -2.43%. The macro backdrop stays two-sided, with the FOMC having raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote while stating that inflation remains elevated, and a 10-year at 5% feeding a standing headwind. The material change this run is geopolitical and arrived after Friday's settle. Overnight into 19 September, Houthi forces struck the Saudi capital - an Aramco fuel storage depot at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport burned after air-raid alerts - and claimed a second operation against Aramco facilities at Yanbu, the Red Sea export gateway whose loadings have been suspended since mid-September and whose feeder East-West pipeline, normally 4-5 million barrels a day and the kingdom's primary Hormuz bypass, has been shut since an 11 September drone attack. Crude had been falling for three sessions into Friday on reports of more Saudi barrels routed via Hormuz, so this strike cuts directly against the move that was in train. Iran itself launched nothing on 19 September and has conveyed negotiating conditions to mediators, leaving the weekend genuinely two-sided. None of it is priceable: it landed in a closed market and must be absorbed in one step at a reopen that sits outside this window. Because the venue is shut throughout, Tail holds its structural floor - there is no mechanism by which mean reversion can fail inside a halted market. Tail eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches a window high of 7 across Sunday afternoon, reflecting accumulating untested headline exposure ahead of an unpriced reopen rather than any observed structure. Stress traces the same shape from a low of 22 to a high of 28. Confidence is solid rather than high: the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified, but it is static, and Friday's marks age through every subsequent hour with no tape able to refresh them.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed triple-witching cash session, then fell through 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final eighteen slots. Stress peaked at 47 in the Friday afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive hours before edging back to 24 across the last two slots. Dominant mode moved from mixed through a single trend-up print at the Friday close into normal for the last 22 hours. Confidence rose to 88 at the close and then declined steadily to 74 as the live tape gave way to the weekend and Friday's marks aged. No hour in the lookback is unavailable.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, four hours after the final slot here. No published hour contains a tradable tape, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window - the next catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday. Tail holds 5 for two hours, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt from 21:00Z Saturday, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday, steps to 6 from 11:00Z and reaches a window high of 7 from 15:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates toward an unpriced reopen. Stress mirrors that shape between a low of 22 and a high of 28, crossing into the moderate band from 11:00Z Sunday. Confidence declines gently from 74 to 66 as Friday's verified marks age. Every step is a function of venue distance and accumulating unpriced information, not of observed price structure; dominant mode stays normal throughout because a halted venue has no structure to classify. Tail is capped at 7 rather than drifting higher because the weekend evidence remains genuinely two-sided: a fresh strike on Riyadh and claimed Aramco targets at Yanbu argue one way, while a tenth consecutive day without an Iranian launch, Iranian negotiating conditions conveyed to mediators and three straight sessions of crude decline argue the other.
